entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Emperor He of Han was the 4th emperor of the Eastern Han and the 20th emperor of the Han dynasty, ruling from 88 to 106. Born into a family of eunuchs during the late Eastern Han, He rose through the ranks by leveraging his connections with powerful figures like Cao Rui, the last emperor of the Eastern Han. His ascension to power was facilitated by his marriage to a woman from the royal family, further solidifying his claim to the throne.

During his reign, Emperor He implemented various policies aimed at restoring economic stability and promoting cultural revitalization. He also strengthened the military, investing in new technologies and strategies to counter threats from neighboring tribes. Notably, he oversaw the construction of several important infrastructure projects, including the expansion of the Grand Canal and the renovation of the Great Wall.

Emperor He's legacy can be seen in the continued prosperity of the Eastern Han under his successors, as well as the lasting impact of his policies on Chinese culture and society. His reign serves as a testament to the enduring influence of imperial rule during this period in Chinese history.

A notable event during his reign was the rebellion led by Gongsun Yuan, a powerful warlord who sought to overthrow Emperor He's government. Despite initial successes, the rebellion ultimately failed, and Gongsun Yuan was defeated by the emperor's forces. This marked a turning point in the Eastern Han dynasty, as the emperor's victory cemented his position as one of the most effective rulers of the period.

In conclusion, Emperor He of Han played a crucial role in shaping the course of Chinese history, leaving behind a lasting legacy that continues to be felt today.
